answer: Proof of replication. For an archive of timber surveys, quill manuscripts, and fable collections, require each storage identity to commit to a full replica encoded with its own key. The verifier samples unpredictable blocks and demands proofs before a short deadline. N rewarded identities then need N stored encodings, costing disk capacity and upkeep. This assumes the encoding is costly enough to regenerate that one shared copy cannot answer all audits in time; deduplication or fast recomputation would defeat the resource bound.
